text:
devon: Heads up — after the CUDA driver bump to 54721 on h100-canary, short-seq (<=8) p99 jumped 4x. Noticed it coincided with autotuner switching to the vectorized small-seq kernel.

maria: Ugh. Numbers?

devon: Before: p50 12ms p95 26ms p99 34ms. After: p50 14ms p95 80ms p99 138ms for seq=8 generation sampling workload. Throughput at same qps dropped ~18%.

aj: Do you have an example trace / kernel pick log?

devon: Pasted snippet from runtime debug log:

```
[2026-03-17T09:12:01Z] request id=... seq_len=8 model=redwood-vicuna-13b kernel=vec_small_seq_v2 arch=h100 driver=54721 autotune_reason=seq_hitrate
[2026-03-17T09:12:01Z] kercall: launch vec_small_seq_v2 grid=(128,1,1) smem=10240 us
[2026-03-17T09:12:01Z] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.18 prefetch=on
```

liam: So autotuner prefers vec_small_seq_v2 now. Was that kernel recently promoted?

maria: We had a kernel patch last week optimizing large-batch throughput that added vectorized code-paths for small seqs too. It passed microbenchmarks but maybe driver changes affected warp scheduling.

nina: perf-bot telemetry shows a spike in warp-stall cycles aligned with the driver rollout window. Also KV cache reuse dropped ~15% for the same prefix distribution.

aj: Could be register pressure or different SM scheduling in 54721 causing vectorized kernel to hit a slowpath. Also vectorized kernels can be worse for KV cache locality if they change memory access stride.

maria: Quick test: can we force the old scalar small-seq kernel and see if latency returns?

devon: I added a runtime override env: FORCE_KERNEL=scalar_small_seq_v1 and re-ran 5k reqs on canary. p99 went back to ~36ms. Throughput recovered. So yes, kernel choice is correlated.

liam: Good repro. That suggests either kernel impl or driver/runtime interaction. Is it only on H100 or also on A100?

devon: Only on H100 instances that got 54721. A100 hosts unchanged.

maria: Ops, can we roll back driver on the canary pool? ops-bot?

ops-bot: @maria To rollback driver on the canary pool run: `ops driver rollback --group=h100-canary --target=54688`. This will cycle instances; expected impact: 3-5 min per host. Confirm to proceed.

nina: Before rolling back, we should triage autotuner thresholds: maybe vectorized kernel selection logic weighted by a heuristic that changed due to micro-bench noise. If we tune away from selecting vec_small_seq_v2 for seq<=12, it avoids regression without infra change.

aj: Agreed. Two parallel actions: 1) temporary rollback on canary to validate fix, 2) revert autotuner pick rule (or add driver-aware exception) and run canary again.

maria: Who can submit the autotuner change?

liam: I'll open a PR: change heuristic to prefer scalar_small_seq_v1 for arch=h100 when seq<=12 OR when driver>=54720. Patch will be small: lower vec kernel score by 30 for that predicate.

devon: I'll coordinate canary rollback test. If rollback to 54688 restores baseline, that's our mitigation. Then liam's autotune patch as medium-term.

maria: Also capture perf counters on failing runs: warp occupancy, sm_efficiency, l2_bw_util. Add to the issue. We need data before blaming driver.

nina: Perf-bot will attach last 6-hour aggregation and the microbench logs to the thread.

perf-bot: Attached: /artifacts/perf/2319876543/summary.json (p99_latency_by_seq.csv, kernel_choice_hist.png).

aj: After rollback, if scalar kernel is good but vectorized still performs better on other drivers, we might need a driver-aware kernel scoring rule rather than a hard disable.

maria: Good point. Longer term: add a driver compatibility test to our CI autotuner jobs — exercise kernels under multiple driver versions in emulated environment.

liam: PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4287 — autotuner heuristic patch + unit test.

devon: Rolling back now on h100-canary (hosts: h100-c1,h100-c2). Will post results in ~10m.

maria: Thanks. Also tagging security/compliance? Not needed, infra-only.

devon: Post-rollback quick numbers: p99 seq=8 returned to 38ms, throughput restored. Kernel choice reverted to scalar_small_seq_v1.

nina: Telemetry shows warp-stall cycles back to baseline and KV cache reuse recovered.

maria: OK shiproom: 1) keep rollback on canary until autotuner patch is deployed to prod canary 2) run extended canary for 6h 3) coordinate with infra to schedule driver rollout pause.

ops-bot: Noted. Rolling plan: hold full rollout until autotuner patch merges + 6h canary green.

aj: Follow-ups: we'll open a root-cause issue to investigate whether vectorized kernel ABI or memory stride interacts with driver 54721 scheduling. Assign to runtime and perf teams.

liam: Assigning to @aj and @devon.

devon: Will add reproducer and kernel microbench results to the issue.

maria: Thanks all. Great quick triage. :thumbsup:

aj: Leaving a note — if we see similar driver-induced shifts again, plan B is to add a lightweight runtime kernel sanity check that runs a tiny microbench at startup and adjusts kernel scores dynamically.

liam: Noted. Filed as RFC-312 in docs.

devon: Thread done for now. Updating incident board.
